title: GET /books/{id} returns 500 instead of 404 for a missing book
evidence: src/repository.rs:66-74 get_book_by_id uses .fetch_one(); a missing row yields sqlx::Error::RowNotFound, propagated by `?` through AppError::Database(#[from] sqlx::Error) (src/lib.rs:8-9) and mapped to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (src/lib.rs:18-19). Route exists and returns a single book for existing ids (src/api.rs:26-33), but the pinned R4 requires 404 if absent. Contrast delete_book (src/repository.rs:99-108) which checks rows_affected and returns AppError::NotFound.
suggestion: In get_book_by_id, map sqlx::Error::RowNotFound to AppError::NotFound (e.g. .fetch_optional() then ok_or(AppError::NotFound)), so a missing id yields 404.

title: PUT /books/{id} on a missing book returns 500 instead of 404
evidence: src/repository.rs:76-97 update_book uses .fetch_one() with RETURNING; updating a non-existent id yields RowNotFound -> AppError::Database -> 500 (src/lib.rs:18-19). R5's pinned how_to_verify only requires modifying an existing book, so this is a related quality gap, not a strict R5 violation.
suggestion: Use .fetch_optional() and return AppError::NotFound when no row matched, mirroring delete_book.
